subject.title: [Feature]: Harden Control UI Lit lifecycle boundaries

question: Should maintainers sponsor this as a dedicated Control UI lifecycle-hardening slice now, and should the first PR cover all listed surfaces or a narrower shell/router/chat subset?
rationale: The issue is protected by the `maintainer` label and proposes an architectural refactor across several UI owners; automation can verify a scoped PR later, but should not choose the product/refactor boundary itself.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow lifecycle slice
options.body: Start with shared Lit base/controller boundaries for the highest-risk shell/router/chat teardown paths and require focused browser or unit teardown proof before widening the pattern.

options.title: Sponsor the full modernization slice
options.body: Allow one larger Control UI refactor covering all listed surfaces, accepting higher review and regression risk for a single coordinated boundary change.

options.title: Defer until a concrete bug PR exists
options.body: Keep the issue open as planning context but wait for a smaller issue or reproducible failure before changing shared UI lifecycle architecture.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow lifecycle slice
recommendation.body: Start with shared Lit base/controller boundaries for the highest-risk shell/router/chat teardown paths and require focused browser or unit teardown proof before widening the pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: Shakker is the strongest current-code routing signal for the sampled Control UI lifecycle files, even though the history is shallow and the issue sponsor may still need to confirm product scope.
